_comment_1: EVERY line the Overseer speaks lives in this file. Keys are looked up by content_loader.resolve_narrative(): a day-specific key wins, then the matching generic_* key below, then a hard-coded last resort in content_loader._LAST_RESORT. Blank a value to fall through to the generic copy.
_comment_foreman: PLAYER-FACING NAME: the Overseer is presented to players as THE FOREMAN (2026-09-24, VOICE_GUIDE.md). Code identifiers, this file's name and every key keep 'overseer'; only text a player can read says Foreman. Every line here is written in the dockside voice — read VOICE_GUIDE.md before editing.
_comment_2: Per-day keys are named by day_NN.json's overseer_intro_key / overseer_outro_keys, and dayN_between by convention. Synthesized days (any day with no day_NN.json) ask for dayN_intro, dayN_outro_<performance> and dayN_between; authoring those keys here is enough to give an unauthored day real copy, no code change needed.
_comment_5b2_days_14_16: #42 Phase 5b-2. Alignment-banded content only — no plain day14_intro/day15_intro/day16_intro/etc. keys are authored. ANY CONSUMER OF THESE DAYS' NARRATIVE KEYS MUST GO THROUGH resolve_aligned_narrative (or otherwise check the three banded variants) — NOT raw dict indexing and NOT the plain resolve_narrative chain, since there is no plain fallback key here for either of those to fall back to. Code review of the first cut of this task (a9e5512) found exactly this: hackdox.py's `simulate` command indexed narratives[day.overseer_intro_key] directly and raised KeyError on every one of these five days; fixed to call resolve_aligned_narrative, and test_every_day_declares_narrative_keys_that_actually_resolve now guards the whole campaign against the same mistake recurring. First stretch of the banded arc: the immediate, then patterned, then confronted aftermath of day 13's crackdown, building toward day 17's own scripted (un-banded) crack.
_comment_5b2_days_18_19: #42 Phase 5b-2. Second and final alignment-banded stretch — same no-plain-fallback-key reasoning as the days-14-16 comment above: any consumer must go through resolve_aligned_narrative (or check all three banded variants), never raw indexing or the plain resolve_narrative chain, since there is no plain day18_intro/day19_intro/etc. key to fall back to. Picks up the morning after day 17's own scripted crack, building toward day 20's bespoke, un-banded send-off. Neither day's copy names a band or quotes an ENDINGS title, matching the discipline test_day_20_overseer_copy_does_not_presume_an_ending enforces for day 20 itself.
generic_intro: Same as yesterday. Read the book, work the gate, and don't let anything off the boat you can't account for.
generic_outro_excellent: Clean shift. Nothing to talk about, which is the best thing I can say about a day on this pier.
generic_outro_passing: That'll do. The line moved and the terminal's still standing.
generic_outro_poor: Something got past you today. I'd rather that didn't turn into a pattern.
generic_outro_failed: Hang back after the whistle. We need to talk about today. Not here.
generic_between: Rest while you can. Tomorrow's boat is fuller, and the book won't be getting any kinder. Spend your HackDollar$ wisely.
day1_intro_friendly:
Welcome to the gate. I'm the Foreman. I'll be straight with you — the whole system's already been hacked. That's why you're here, doing this by hand, like we did it before the machines.
Here's the shape of it. People come to the gate wanting in. You decide who gets off the boat. Every one you wave through that shouldn't have been, the site takes damage — that's the number in the corner, and if it hits zero we're both out of work.
Today you have their papers — the dossier — and nothing else. Read it, and cast a verdict. The rulebook is on the R key. Use it.
And watch the clock — that's ⏱, your hours for the day. You'll want them later. We'll talk again at the whistle.
day1_outro_praise: Good shift. The line moved, the right people got in, the wrong people didn't. That's all anybody on this pier asks.
day1_outro_measured: You're learning. Tomorrow's faster. Keep your eyes open and your fingers clear.
day1_outro_warning: You let one slip through. We notice. Don't make a habit of it.
day1_outro_failed: Hang back after the whistle. You and me need to talk about what you let off the boat today.
day1_between: Not bad for a first shift. The site held. Listen — the pay you earned tonight, the HackDollars, you spend them here. Tools get cheaper, the terminal gets smarter. And those Credits? Ground truth on demand. Save them for when you truly cannot call it. Tomorrow the line gets longer.
day2_intro:
You read a dossier well enough. Problem is, a dossier is whatever they typed into it. Paper's cheap.
So today you get to check. Ghostscan asks around the docks for you — where their handle turns up, whether the organisation on their form is the organisation on their profiles, and whether their email is sitting in a breach corpus. That last one is the panel on the right; it's a fixed list, so learn it and it stops costing you time.
It isn't free. Nothing on this pier is. Spend the hours where the dossier already made you suspicious, not on everyone.
day2_outro_excellent: You used the tool where it mattered and left it on the hook where it didn't. That's the whole job.
day2_outro_passing: Reasonable. You're still scanning people the dossier had already answered for you, but you'll stop.
day2_outro_poor: You've got a tool now and something still walked past you. Use it.
day2_outro_failed: Two days. I'd like to say I'm surprised.
day2_between: One more list on that panel soon. It grows, it doesn't change — anything you learn tonight is still true next week.
day3_intro:
Everyone who comes to the gate submits a credential. Hashcrack tells you what it's worth — think of it as prying the lid off a sealed crate.
Three things to know. The algorithm is on the dossier already, free — bcrypt is solid, SHA256 is middling, MD5 is a cardboard box. Then there's what the password actually is, and for that you have to crack it. A weak password is sloppiness. A password sitting in a breach corpus is something else.
The log also shows you where they logged in from. Compare it to what they claimed. People forget that part.
day3_outro_excellent: You cracked the ones worth cracking. bcrypt is never worth cracking, and you clearly worked that out.
day3_outro_passing: Fine. You're spending hours prying at hashes that told you everything from the chip alone.
day3_outro_poor: A bad password isn't a crime. A breached one is. You're not separating them.
day3_between: A second breach corpus is live as of today. Reused passwords show up in more than one — that's the tell.
day4_intro:
Logwatch. Think of it as the logbook. It opens on a report of your applicant's day — bars, a timeline, where they logged in from. That part is free. Read it first.
The raw log costs you, and it doesn't hand you your applicant: it's the whole day's traffic, every account, sorted by time. Finding their lines in it is the skill.
What you're looking for: a wall of failed logins, access at hours nobody works, or two logins from places nobody could travel between in the time. Any of those, from their account, and you have your answer.
day4_outro_excellent: You found them in the noise. Most new hands take a week to do that.
day4_outro_passing: You got there. Slowly, but you got there.
day4_outro_poor: The evidence was in the log. You didn't go down and get it.
day4_outro_failed: We're done for today. Don't come back tomorrow assuming you still have a spot on this gate.
day4_between: Last tool tomorrow. Then you'll have the full kit, and I'll stop explaining things.
day5_intro:
Last one. Some of them submit an image with their papers, and some of those images have a false bottom.
Stegotool. Press X for stamp mode, arrows to move, Space to stamp — one hour a stamp, so aim. When you hit carrier data the signature colours tell you what's in the hold: amber is plaintext, crimson is encrypted, violet is a command-and-control beacon. That last one is not an accident and not a mistake.
Stamp where the image looks wrong, not everywhere.
day5_outro_excellent: Good. You found it without stamping the picture into confetti.
day5_outro_passing: You got there. Watch the hours — every stamp is one.
day5_outro_poor: Something went off the boat today with contraband in the hold.
day5_outro_failed: That's five days and I'm still having this conversation at the whistle.
day5_graduation:
That's everything. Every piece of gear you're getting, you have.
From here I stop walking you through it. The rulebook is still the rulebook, but it changes — sometimes overnight, and I'll tell you when it does, though not always with much notice.
And the ones at the gate get better at this. The obvious ones thin out. What's left are the ones who know exactly what you check.
Good luck. Mind your fingers.
day5_between: You're through the training days. Tomorrow the line is longer, the tools cost more, and nobody is going to tell you which page to open. Spend what you earned.
day6_intro:
Seven today. No new tool, no new page — you've got the full kit now, so use what's already on the desk before you decide.
No new lines in the book either. One of the old ones shifted on its moorings, though — I'll get to it in a second.
Work the gate. I'm not walking the line with you anymore.
day6_outro_excellent: Clean. That's the standard now, not a bonus.
day6_outro_passing: It held. Not fast, but it held.
day6_outro_poor: Something got through that the rulebook would have caught, if you'd opened it.
day6_outro_failed: That's not what I needed from today. We'll talk tomorrow, before the first boat.
day6_between: Same rules tomorrow, more of them to actually apply. Spend what you earned — you'll want the head start.
day7_intro:
Seven again. You'll notice some of today's papers are spotless — dossier clean, sweep clean, log clean, nothing anywhere you're required to look.
Spotless isn't the same question as fine. It just means the checklist ran out before it found anything.
If it's genuinely clean, clear it. That's still the rule. Go on.
day7_outro_excellent: That's the read I want. You didn't mistake spotless for fine, and you didn't invent problems that weren't there either.
day7_outro_passing: You got through it. A couple of those deserved a second look before you waved them on.
day7_outro_poor: Something walked off the boat today with nothing on its papers. That's not innocence — that's a gap in your read.
day7_outro_failed: Twice in two days. I don't want a third.
day7_between: Two shifts past training and the line keeps growing. So does what I expect out of you. Spend it, rest your back, and be sharper tomorrow.
day8_intro:
Before you start — I've got something to read you. It's not mine, I didn't draft it, and I'd rather not be the one saying it out loud. But it came down from upstairs, so it's the book now.
Nothing else moved today. Same faces at the gate as always. Work the line.
day8_outro_excellent: You didn't let the new softness slow you down. Good — I wasn't sure you'd notice the difference.
day8_outro_passing: It held. Even with the book riding a little lighter in the water than it was yesterday.
day8_outro_poor: Something got a pass today that yesterday's book would have caught. That's what 'advisory' costs you, apparently.
day8_outro_failed: That line cost us today, on the first day it existed. I'll put it in the log. I'm honestly not sure who reads it.
day8_between: Spend it. Tomorrow's book won't be any heavier — I wouldn't get used to that.
day9_intro:
Another one came down this morning. Same shape as yesterday's, different line. I've worked this pier long enough to know a pattern when one ties up next to me.
Read it, then get to work.
day9_outro_excellent: Two soft spots in the book now and you still read them right. Don't let that turn into a habit you stop noticing.
day9_outro_passing: You got through it. I'd have liked cleaner, but the book's not any cleaner either, is it.
day9_outro_poor: Yesterday's softness, today's mistake. I'm noticing a shape here and I don't love it.
day9_outro_failed: Two directives in, and we're already having the bad version of this conversation at the whistle.
day9_between: Spend what you've got. I'd tell you the tide turns from here, but you've read the same book I have.
day10_intro:
Three now. I stopped asking why around directive two. Compliance says it's about false-positive rates. I have my own read on who's paying compliance's wages, but nobody's asked for it.
Anyway. Work the gate.
day10_outro_excellent: Clean, in spite of everything upstairs keeps taking off the table. That's on you, not the book.
day10_outro_passing: Held. Barely, and less because of the rules than because of you.
day10_outro_poor: Three lines gone soft this week, and today's the day one of them mattered. Of course it was today.
day10_outro_failed: I don't have anything reassuring left to say about how this book keeps drifting. Neither should you.
day10_between: Spend it while it's still yours to spend. I wouldn't assume tomorrow's tide does you any favours either.
day11_intro:
Fourth one. Read it yourself — I'm done pretending to be surprised by these.
Here's what I actually think, since you keep looking at me like I owe you an explanation: every one of these makes your job easier, not harder. Fewer deny calls, fewer arguments at the gate, fewer people looking at you sideways when you turn them back. Everybody on this pier eats when the boats keep moving. You should be thanking upstairs, not glaring at me.
Work the line. And stop looking for someone in this shed to be angry at.
day11_outro_excellent: You read straight through four directives without flinching once. I'd call that discipline. Some people upstairs would call it something else.
day11_outro_passing: You got there. Try not to let a fifth one — whenever it comes — slow you down the way the third one did.
day11_outro_poor: Something walked off the boat today on a rule I personally handed you the softened version of. I did my part.
day11_outro_failed: Four days of me making this easier for you, and today's the day it fell apart. That's not the book's fault anymore. That one's yours.
day11_between: Spend it. And think about what you're actually protecting by still holding the line on the one rule nobody's asked you to soften yet — because I promise you, somebody's noticed that you do.
day12_intro:
Before you touch the stack — somebody upstairs has taken an interest in one of today's names. Not which one. Not why. Just that they want to know how you call it.
I'll tell you what I told myself the first time this happened to me on this gate: it's still your line, still your rules, still your signature at the bottom. Whatever's in there isn't going to announce itself. And if it trips the one rule I already told you nobody's softened, don't mistake that for a coincidence. You're going to have to actually work for this one.
Read carefully. I mean that more today than I usually do.
day12_outro_excellent: Clean stack, quota cleared, health untouched. Whoever upstairs was watching today got their answer. I don't know yet if they liked it — and for once, I'm glad that's not mine to explain.
day12_outro_passing: You got through it. Something in that stack didn't sit clean by the end, and I have a guess which one it was. I'm not going to say which. I don't think I need to.
day12_outro_poor: Short today, on the one day I told you to look harder than usual. I don't know if the two are related. I have a guess.
day12_outro_failed: I told you somebody was watching the gate. I never said it would go easy on you if you got it wrong. Today, you got it wrong.
day12_between: Spend it. Whatever you decided about the name I couldn't tell you about — it's done now, it's in the log, and it isn't coming back off it. I hope you're as sure about it as you looked.
day13_intro:
Whatever happened yesterday, it isn't staying in yesterday. Upstairs wants a name for how close that was, and since nobody's handing them one, they're battening down every seam it could have used instead.
There's a new line in the book below. Read it before you touch the queue — I'm not going to enjoy saying it out loud, so I'm not saying it twice.
Work the gate. And don't ask me if this is really about security anymore. I'm not sure I'd like my own answer.
day13_outro_excellent: Clean stack, on the one day I genuinely didn't know what I wanted from you. Take the win. I'm not going to pretend I understand why it matters to me that you got it.
day13_outro_passing: You got through it. Nobody upstairs is going to call today a problem. I'm choosing to leave it there.
day13_outro_poor: Short today, the same week we tightened the one rule that was supposed to catch exactly this. Draw your own conclusions. I already have.
day13_outro_failed: I handed you a stricter book and an actual reason for it, and today still came apart at the seams. I don't have a second explanation in me.
day13_between: Spend it. Whatever's coming next, it isn't going to feel like yesterday got resolved. It's going to feel like yesterday is still happening, just slower — like fog that won't lift.
day14_whitehat_intro:
You didn't wait for me to tell you the new line applies to more than encryption. Three separate calls yesterday where the rulebook would've let something off the boat and you didn't let it — nobody asked you to go further than what's written.
I'm not going to pretend that's not useful to me. I'm also not going to pretend it doesn't make you a very specific kind of visible, to people who are already looking harder than they were a week ago.
Work the gate. And maybe don't make today the day you go looking for a fourth.
day14_whitehat_outro_excellent: Clean, and every deny you made stayed inside the line instead of past it. That restraint isn't nothing — I noticed it, even if I'm not going to say why.
day14_whitehat_outro_passing: You got there. Same as yesterday — reading further into the book than it strictly asks. I keep waiting for that to become a problem. It hasn't yet.
day14_whitehat_outro_poor: Something got through, on a day you'd otherwise have caught it on principle alone. Even you have a rough shift, apparently. Good to know.
day14_whitehat_outro_failed: I expected today to go worse for someone else's reasons, not yours. That's almost more unsettling than if it hadn't surprised me at all.
day14_whitehat_between: Spend it. And do it quietly — the version of you that keeps reading past the line is exactly the version upstairs would notice first, if anyone up there were paying the kind of attention I am.
day14_neutral_intro:
No extra weight on the new line yesterday, no argument about it either. You read it, you applied it, you moved on to the next name like it was any other Tuesday at the gate.
I don't know what to do with that, if I'm honest. Everyone who's ever sat where you're sitting either fights the book or hides behind it. You do neither. You just work it.
Work the line. I'll let you know if I figure out which one that actually is.
day14_neutral_outro_excellent: Clean stack, worked exactly to the letter, same as every letter before it. I still can't tell if that's discipline or just an absence of anything else.
day14_neutral_outro_passing: You got there, going by the book the whole way. Consistent, I'll give you that. Consistent toward what, I genuinely couldn't say.
day14_neutral_outro_poor: Something got past the letter today. Not past you specifically — past the rule itself, which I suppose isn't your fault. I'm not sure whose it is.
day14_neutral_outro_failed: You followed the book and the book still lost today. I don't know if that's an argument against the book or against pretending it was ever enough on its own.
day14_neutral_between: Spend it. You're the one person on this pier I can't predict from one day to the next, and somehow that's because you never do anything unpredictable at all.
day14_darkweb_intro:
You clocked the new line yesterday morning and didn't say a word about it — not a complaint, not a question, not even the look everyone else on this gate still gives me. Just did the job like the last softened rule and this stricter one were the same instruction.
I don't have to explain myself to you anymore, do I. That's — actually easier than I expected it to be.
Work the gate. I mean that more comfortably today than I usually do, and I'd rather not think too hard about why.
day14_darkweb_outro_excellent: Clean. Efficient. You didn't even need the stricter line spelled out twice — you'd already priced it in before I said anything. That should probably worry me more than it does.
day14_darkweb_outro_passing: You got there. Didn't ask me to justify a single call today. I'm starting to like that about you more than I probably should.
day14_darkweb_outro_poor: Something got through. Not going to pretend I'm losing sleep over it, and I don't think you are either. That's new, for both of us.
day14_darkweb_outro_failed: Rough one. Six months ago I'd have had a speech ready for this at the whistle. Today I just don't feel like giving it, and I don't think you're expecting one.
day14_darkweb_between: Spend it. I'm not going to sell you on caution tonight — you've stopped needing it, and honestly, so have I.
day15_whitehat_intro:
Yesterday wasn't a one-off. I went back through the logbook — you've been reading every soft line in this book like it's a suggestion, not a floor. That's not caution. That's a pattern, and patterns get noticed eventually, by people who aren't me.
I keep telling myself it isn't my job to warn you about that. I keep doing it anyway. Draw your own conclusions about what that means.
Work the line. Today's stack doesn't care what either of us has decided about the other.
day15_whitehat_outro_excellent: Clean, and consistent with everything you've shown me this week. I'd call it admirable if I were in a position to say that out loud to anyone but you.
day15_whitehat_outro_passing: You got there. Same restraint, same margin above the letter of the book. I'm running out of ways to say that without it sounding like approval.
day15_whitehat_outro_poor: One got through today. First crack in the hull after a week of reading harder than the book asks. Even a pattern breaks somewhere.
day15_whitehat_outro_failed: Today's the day the pattern I've been watching didn't hold. I won't pretend I'm not disappointed — mostly in the timing.
day15_whitehat_between: Spend it. I keep almost telling you to be careful, and then remembering that telling you that would mean admitting I've been watching closely enough to have an opinion.
day15_neutral_intro:
Second day running, no lean either way. I've started keeping a tally, which probably says more about me than it does about you.
Everybody I've ever handed this book to eventually decides what they actually think of it — sooner or later, whether they admit it or not. You're the first one who hasn't, and I can't decide if that's patience or something closer to nothing at all.
Work the gate. I'll keep watching either way.
day15_neutral_outro_excellent: Clean, by the letter, same as always. I used to find that reassuring. Today it mostly just made me curious.
day15_neutral_outro_passing: You got there, exactly the way you get through everything — no flourish, no argument, no tell. I'd love to know what that costs you. I don't expect you to say.
day15_neutral_outro_poor: Something slipped past the book today, and I can't even blame you for reading it wrong — you read it exactly right. The book was just wrong first.
day15_neutral_outro_failed: The letter of it failed you today, and you followed the letter right up until it did. I don't know what lesson you're supposed to take from that. Maybe there isn't one.
day15_neutral_between: Spend it. I've stopped trying to guess which way you're actually leaning. At this point I think that not-knowing might be the most honest thing left on this pier.
day15_darkweb_intro:
You've stopped even glancing at the softened lines before you apply them. That's not a complaint — if anything it's saving us both time on the clock. I just noticed, and I'm apparently the kind of person who mentions things like that to you now.
I used to rehearse a version of this speech where I sound sorry about all of it. I don't think I need it anymore, with you. That's either a relief or the worst thing I've admitted all week. I haven't decided.
Work the line. I trust you to know what that means today better than I want to spell out.
day15_darkweb_outro_excellent: Nothing wasted today — you moved the stack faster than the old book would ever have let you. I keep telling myself that's just efficiency.
day15_darkweb_outro_passing: You got there. No hesitation anywhere in the stack that I could see. I've stopped expecting to see any.
day15_darkweb_outro_poor: One slipped through today. Neither of us is going to pretend that's a crisis. That's the part I should probably still find strange.
day15_darkweb_outro_failed: Today didn't hold together. I'm not going to dress it up as a moral failure, mine or yours. We're a bit past that particular fiction, aren't we.
day15_darkweb_between: Spend it. I like this version of the conversation better than the one where I have to talk you into anything. You already know.
day16_whitehat_intro:
You're becoming a liability. I need you to hear that plainly, because I'm not going to be able to say it as plainly again after today: every call you make past what the book requires is a call somebody upstairs could eventually trace back to me for letting stand.
I don't know why I'm still the one saying it instead of just writing you up and finding a new clerk. I've had chances. I keep not taking them.
Work the gate. And for once, I'm not going to tell you to be careful. I think we both know you've already decided you're not going to be.
day16_whitehat_outro_excellent: Clean stack, on a day I half expected to be the one where this finally caught up with both of us. It didn't. I don't know whether to be relieved or more worried.
day16_whitehat_outro_passing: You got there. I keep waiting for the day this stops working out for you. Today wasn't it. I don't think that means much, long haul.
day16_whitehat_outro_poor: Something got through, the same week I told you plainly what you're risking. I don't know if that makes today better or worse for either of us.
day16_whitehat_outro_failed: I warned you what today could cost you, and today cost you anyway, just not the way I meant. That's not comforting to either of us.
day16_whitehat_between: Spend it. I don't have anything left to add tonight that I haven't already said too plainly once today.
day16_neutral_intro:
I said something to someone yesterday I probably shouldn't have — not to you, to somebody who isn't you, and it's been sitting badly with me since. I don't know why I'm telling you that. Maybe because you're the one person who won't do anything with it either way.
Everybody else on this pier either performs loyalty at me or performs doubt at me, depending on the day. You don't perform anything. I don't know what that actually costs you, and I've stopped expecting you to tell me.
Work the line. Today's stack, same as every other one — you'll read it, you'll call it, and I still won't be able to tell you what any of it means to you.
day16_neutral_outro_excellent: Clean. By the book, all the way through, same as it's been for two weeks. I keep expecting that to stop meaning anything to me. It hasn't yet.
day16_neutral_outro_passing: You got there. I don't have anything new to say about how — you know how you do it as well as I do by now.
day16_neutral_outro_poor: Something slipped past today. I don't think it changes what I think of how you work. I'm just not entirely sure what that is yet.
day16_neutral_outro_failed: Today didn't go the way either of us wanted, and I still can't tell you which way that was for you. I'm not sure that's ever going to change.
day16_neutral_between: Spend it. I've started finding your silence on all of this restful, which probably says something uncomfortable about the rest of my week.
day16_darkweb_intro:
I said too much to someone yesterday — not you, somebody else, somebody who's going to remember it wrong and use it against me eventually. You wouldn't do that. That's not a compliment exactly. It's just the truest thing I know about you at this point.
I don't know when 'you wouldn't do that' became the nicest thing I have to say about anyone left on this pier, you included. I said it anyway.
Work the gate. You know the shape of it by now as well as I do.
day16_darkweb_outro_excellent: Not a single hitch today. I don't have it in me to dress that up as anything more than what it was.
day16_darkweb_outro_passing: You got there. I'm not going to pretend today took much out of either of us. It didn't.
day16_darkweb_outro_poor: A little got past the tally today. I'll log it and move on — neither of us needed telling twice.
day16_darkweb_outro_failed: That one got away from me. I said my piece about caring, days ago, to somebody else — I don't have a fresh version of it for you tonight.
day16_darkweb_between: Spend it. I'm tired in a way tonight that has nothing to do with the shop or my back, and you're the only one here I don't have to explain that to.
day17_intro:
Five days since the book grew teeth again, and nothing's slipped through it since. Upstairs should be thrilled. I keep waiting to feel thrilled myself, and it isn't coming.
I used to think this job was about keeping the terminal clean. I don't know when it turned into keeping my own hands clean by proxy — flag this, deny that, never once ask what any of it costs the people on the other side of the gate. You get to not think about that. Twenty-odd years on this pier, and I don't have that luxury anymore.
Work the line. Today's stack doesn't care what either of us is feeling about it.
day17_outro_excellent: Clean. Quota cleared. I almost said 'good' out loud like it meant something to me again. Don't get used to that.
day17_outro_passing: You got there. I keep expecting one of these shifts to feel like enough. It never quite does, for either of us, I'd guess.
day17_outro_poor: Something got through today, and for once I'm not going to pretend upstairs is the only one who's disappointed.
day17_outro_failed: I don't have the energy to make this sound like your failure alone. It isn't, and today proved it.
day17_between: Spend it. I'm not in the mood to sell you on the shop today. Buy what you need and go — I've got my own accounting to do tonight.
day18_whitehat_intro:
I said more yesterday than I meant to. You didn't do anything with it — didn't push, didn't ask follow-up, didn't file it away to use against me later the way I half expected. I don't know what to make of that yet, but I noticed.
Maybe that's the closest thing to solidarity either of us gets on this pier. I'm not going to call it that out loud twice.
Work the gate. Today's just a shift. I'd like at least one more of those before whatever's coming actually comes.
day18_whitehat_outro_excellent: Clean. After yesterday, I didn't expect to feel anything about a clean stack again so soon. Turns out I still can.
day18_whitehat_outro_passing: You got there. Thank you for not making yesterday weirder than it already was. I mean that plainly, for once.
day18_whitehat_outro_poor: Something got through, the day after I said more than I should have. I don't think the two are related. I'm choosing to believe that.
day18_whitehat_outro_failed: Today fell apart, right after I opened a door I don't usually leave open. I don't know which one of us that's worse for.
day18_whitehat_between: Spend it. I'm not going to pretend yesterday didn't happen, and I'm not going to bring it up again either. Just — thank you for not making me regret it more than I already do.
day18_neutral_intro:
I said something out loud yesterday I don't usually let myself say, to you specifically, and I still don't know why — you're not going to use it, and you're not going to comfort me with it either. You're just going to do the job, like you always do.
I think that might be exactly why I said it to you. There's nowhere for it to go from here but out with the tide.
Work the line. Same as yesterday. Same as tomorrow, probably.
day18_neutral_outro_excellent: Clean, the day after I said too much. I don't know what to do with that except say it went fine. It went fine.
day18_neutral_outro_passing: You got there. Whatever I said yesterday, it didn't change how you work today. I think that's the most honest response anyone could've given it.
day18_neutral_outro_poor: Something got through today. I'd like to blame yesterday for the distraction. I don't think that's actually true.
day18_neutral_outro_failed: Rough one, the day after I let something slip I don't usually let slip. I don't have a theory connecting the two. Maybe there isn't one.
day18_neutral_between: Spend it. I said something yesterday I can't take back, to someone who isn't going to do anything with it either way. I think that's the only reason I could say it at all.
day18_darkweb_intro:
I let something slip yesterday I don't usually let slip, and you didn't even blink. Didn't ask what it meant, didn't file it away. I keep telling myself that's because you already knew.
It's easier with you than with anyone else I deal with on this pier. I'm aware of how that sounds. I'm saying it anyway.
Work the gate. I don't have it in me today to make this sound like more than a Tuesday.
day18_darkweb_outro_excellent: Smooth one, right after yesterday. I don't need to dress it up as anything more than a good shift.
day18_darkweb_outro_passing: You got there. I appreciate that you didn't make yesterday into a bigger thing than it needed to be. Not everyone I work with would've let it go that easily.
day18_darkweb_outro_poor: A borderline one got past today. Small thing, after the bigger thing yesterday. I'm not going to pretend I have room to be upset about it.
day18_darkweb_outro_failed: Today slipped, the day after I said more than I meant to. I don't think either of those is really about the other. I could be wrong.
day18_darkweb_between: Spend it. Thanks for not making yesterday into something. I don't say that to people anymore. I just said it to you.
day19_whitehat_intro:
One more after today. I keep almost telling you what I think you're going to do with whatever you walk off this pier holding — and then remembering that's not mine to say, and probably never was.
Whatever happens tomorrow, I want it in the log that I saw what you were doing, this whole stretch. I'm not saying that as a threat. I don't think I need to explain why that matters, if it does.
Work the gate. One more after this one, and then we'll both find out what it added up to.
day19_whitehat_outro_excellent: Clean, with one shift left after this. I don't know what I'm hoping for tomorrow. I know what I'm not hoping for, and that might be enough of an answer.
day19_whitehat_outro_passing: You got there. Same as every day you've made this harder for yourself than the book asked. I don't think I ever thanked you for that. Consider this the closest I get.
day19_whitehat_outro_poor: Something got through, the day before the last one. I'd rather that not be how this stretch is remembered. I don't get to decide that either.
day19_whitehat_outro_failed: Rough one, this close to the end. I don't have anything reassuring left in me. I'm not sure I'd trust it if I did.
day19_whitehat_between: Spend it. Whatever you're saving it for, spend it before tomorrow — there isn't going to be a day after that to regret not using it.
day19_neutral_intro:
One more after today, and I still don't know what you actually think of any of this. Nineteen shifts, and you've never once told me which way you'd have gone if nobody was grading you on it.
I used to mind that not-knowing about you every day. Now it's starting to feel like it might be the whole answer, not a gap in it.
Work the line. Last real shift before the last shift.
day19_neutral_outro_excellent: Clean, with one shift left. I don't know what conclusion you're building toward. I'm starting to think maybe there isn't one, and that maybe that's fine.
day19_neutral_outro_passing: You got there, exactly like every other day. I've stopped waiting for that to change. I think I might miss it, whatever it turns out to have been.
day19_neutral_outro_poor: Something got through, this close to the end. I don't have a read on whether that's you slipping or the book finally running out of pier. Possibly both.
day19_neutral_outro_failed: Rough one, one day before the last one. I don't have a tidy read on what that means for you. I'm not sure I ever did.
day19_neutral_between: Spend it. Tomorrow's the last one, and I still can't tell you which way I think you're going to go. Maybe that's the most honest thing I'll ever say to you.
day19_darkweb_intro:
One more after today. I'm not going to perform suspense about how tomorrow goes — that was never really my register with you. I don't get to call it decided before it's decided, and neither do you.
I used to think watching someone else get this far would make me feel something. Mostly it just makes me tired, the way the end of a long haul does. That's not a complaint.
Work the gate. Last real shift before the last shift. You know what that means as well as I do.
day19_darkweb_outro_excellent: Clean, one shift out from the end. I don't need to dress that up as anything more than a good shift — it doesn't decide anything by itself, and we both know that much.
day19_darkweb_outro_passing: You got there. Same as every day this stretch. I stopped being surprised by that a while ago, and honestly, I stopped needing to be.
day19_darkweb_outro_poor: Small thing got past, this close to the end. Doesn't tell either of us anything we didn't already half expect.
day19_darkweb_outro_failed: Not a good one, one day out. I don't have it in me to make this sound like a crisis — not with tomorrow still an open question, for both of us.
day19_darkweb_between: Spend it. Last night before the last shift. I'm not going to pretend that means anything different for either of us than any other night has.
day20_intro:
Last one. Twenty mornings of me handing you a book that kept changing shape, and twenty mornings of you reading it anyway. Whatever you've made of that is yours now — I stopped being able to predict it a while back.
I'm not going to tell you what to look for today. You know the shapes by now better than I ever taught you to. Whatever's sitting in this stack, you'll see it or you won't, and either way it's the last one I get to say that about.
Work the gate. This is the whole thing, right here. Make of it whatever you're going to make of it.
day20_outro_excellent: Clean stack, quota cleared, on the last shift it was ever going to matter. Whatever this pier made of you, it made something. I'll leave it there.
day20_outro_passing: You got there. Twenty shifts, and you got through every one of them. That's not nothing, whatever else turns out to be true.
day20_outro_poor: Short, on the last day. I won't pretend that doesn't sting a little, for reasons that are probably more mine than yours at this point.
day20_outro_failed: Twenty days, and it comes apart on the last one. I don't have a tidy line for that at the whistle. Maybe there isn't one.
